summary: FBI originated as Bureau of Investigation created 1908 under Attorney General Charles Bonaparte. Renamed Federal Bureau of Investigation 1935 under J. Edgar Hoover who directed it 1924-1972, 48 years. Started with 34 agents, now over 35,000.

J. Edgar Hoover ran FBI 1924-1972, 48 years, through 8 presidents. Built FBI into powerful institution. Used secret files on politicians for leverage. COINTELPRO domestic surveillance program 1956-1971 targeted civil rights leaders, anti-war activists, feminists. FBI abused power under his leadership.

COINTELPRO 1956-1971: FBI counterintelligence program targeting domestic political groups. Tactics: infiltration, psychological warfare, legal harassment, extralegal force. Targeted MLK, Black Panthers, anti-war movement, feminism. Sent letter urging MLK to suicide. Exposed by citizen burglary of FBI office 1971. Church Committee confirmed 1975.

FBI Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list started March 14 1950. Created after reporter asked about toughest guys. 531 fugitives placed on list, 494 captured (94%). 163 captured through public tips. List generates public cooperation. Most famous: James Earl Ray, Ted Bundy, Osama bin Laden, Whitey Bulger.

FBI Behavioral Science Unit at Quantico developed criminal profiling 1970s. John Douglas and Robert Ressler interviewed 36 serial killers to build classification system. Organized vs disorganized crime scenes. Profiling influenced investigation strategy but scientific validity debated. Led to Silence of the Lambs popularization.

FBI Uniform Crime Reporting program collects crime data from 18,000+ agencies. UCR since 1930, replaced by NIBRS 2021. NIBRS captures 24 offense categories with details vs UCR's summary counts. Underreporting is a known limitation. FBI publishes Crime in the United States annually.

FBI National Instant Criminal Background Check System (NICS) launched November 30 1998. Processes firearm purchase background checks. Over 300 million checks through 2023. Denial rate 1.2%. 72% of checks completed instantly. FBI does not maintain gun purchase records per Firearm Owners Protection Act.

FBI Cyber Division created 2002 post-9/11. Investigates computer intrusions, online predation, IP theft, dark web marketplaces. IC3 (Internet Crime Complaint Center) receives complaints. 2023: $12.5B reported cyber losses. FBI can technically attribute attacks through malware analysis, infrastructure tracing, and threat actor TTP patterns.

FBI is lead US counterintelligence agency. Protects US from foreign espionage. Key cases: Robert Hanssen FBI agent who spied for Russia 1979-2001 (most damaging insider in FBI history), Aldrich Ames CIA (co-investigated with CIA). FBI CI Division works with CIA on joint threat assessment.

Robert Hanssen FBI agent spied for USSR/Russia 1979-2001. Sold 6,000 pages of classified documents, revealed US nuclear secrets, disclosed 3 KGB informants executed. Used dead drops. FBI paid $7M to source who identified him. Arrested 2001. Pleaded guilty. Life in prison. Most damaging FBI mole in history.

FBI Joint Terrorism Task Forces (JTTFs) in 56 field offices combine federal state and local investigators. Created 1980s, expanded after 9/11. Over 4,000 investigators. JTTFs share intelligence and coordinate investigations. Post-9/11 reform: better sharing with CIA and NSA. Some concerns about civil liberties and surveillance of communities.

Crossfire Hurricane was FBI investigation into Trump campaign Russia contacts 2016-2017. Opened July 31 2016. DOJ IG report 2019 found investigation properly predicated but FISA applications had 17 significant errors and omissions. Carter Page surveillance flawed. FBI's credibility on FISA damaged.

PATRIOT Act 2001 expanded FBI surveillance powers: roving wiretaps, sneak and peek warrants, National Security Letters without court approval. NSLs include gag orders. FBI issued 192,000 NSLs 2003-2006. Some provisions permanent 2006. Section 215 bulk telephone metadata collection exposed by Snowden 2013.

FBI Carnivore system 1990s-2000s intercepted email and internet traffic at ISP level. Installed as packet sniffer. Name changed to DCS1000 after bad publicity. Raised privacy concerns. Replaced by commercial tools. Demonstrated FBI's early adoption of bulk digital surveillance techniques.

FBI Next Generation Identification (NGI) system replaced IAFIS 2014. World's largest biometric database: 100M+ fingerprints, 50M+ face photos, iris scans, palm prints. Face Recognition pilot matches faces against 400M+ photos. Privacy concerns: no consent, racial bias, accuracy rates. FBI says no policy prohibits face matching.

InfraGard: FBI-private sector partnership for critical infrastructure protection. 70,000+ members across 77 chapters. Members get FBI threat briefings, secure portal access, and information sharing. Criticized as corporate surveillance pipeline. No background check required for membership. Demonstrates FBI's outreach model for cyber threat intelligence.

FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) launched May 8 2000. Receives public complaints of cyber crime. 2023: 880,418 complaints, $12.5B losses. Reports analyzed for patterns, referred to field offices. Annual Internet Crime Report published. IC3 is primary public entry point for FBI cyber crime reporting.

FBI has 56 field offices in major cities, 350+ smaller resident agencies. Each field office has cyber squad, counterintelligence squad, violent crime squad, public corruption squad. New York is largest. Each reports to FBI HQ Washington DC. Field offices have autonomy on case priorities within national guidelines.

FBI Academy at Quantico Virginia trains all special agents. 20-week program: academics, firearms, defensive tactics, operational skills, integrated case scenario. New agents complete Hogan's Alley simulated town. In-service training for 35,000 employees. Behavioral Science Unit located here since 1972.

FBI Sentinel case management system deployed 2012 after Sentinel program cost $451M over 4 years late. Replaced paper-based ACS. Sentinel 2.0 cloud migration 2016. Still criticized for slow search and poor integration. Demonstrates government IT challenge: building operational systems at scale under oversight constraints.

Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) approves FISA warrants for national security surveillance. 11 judges, secret court. 2022: FISA Section 702 reauthorized. FBI queried 702 database for US persons 3.2M times in 2021. Reforms limited queries but debate continues. FISC is the check on FBI's most sensitive surveillance power.

FBI is lead agency for domestic terrorism investigations. Categories: racially motivated violent extremism, anti-government anti-authority violent extremism, animal rights environmental extremism, abortion-related extremism. Post-Jan 6 2021 focus on anti-government extremism. Challenge: balancing investigation with First Amendment protected activity.

FBI Public Corruption program investigates federal state and local officials: bribery, kickbacks, election fraud, contract fraud. 1000+ agents. Key cases: Rod Blagojevich, Bob McDonnell, Dennis Hastert. FBI works with US Attorney offices. Public corruption cases require wiretaps, cooperators, and financial analysis.

FBI Evidence Response Teams (ERTs) in every field office process crime scenes. Specialized in WMD, mass casualty, underwater, disaster recovery. FBI Lab at Quantico is largest forensic lab in world. Handles DNA, fingerprints, ballistics, explosives, trace evidence. Accredited by ASCLD/LAB. FBI forensics sets national standards.

FBI Civil Rights program investigates hate crimes, color of law violations (police misconduct), human trafficking, involuntary servitude, freedom of access to clinic entrances. 1900+ cases open annually. Post-George Floyd 2020: increased police misconduct cases. Tension between FBI as investigator of police and FBI as law enforcement partner.

FBI Organized Crime program targets La Cosa Nostra (Italian mafia), MS-13, cartels, Russian organized crime, Asian organized crime. RICO Act 1970 was key weapon: pattern of racketeering. FBI flipped mobsters: Joe Valachi 1963 first to publicly testify. John Gotti convicted 1992 through FBI surveillance and Sammy Gravano cooperation.

FBI White Collar Crime program investigates corporate fraud, securities fraud, health care fraud, mortgage fraud, money laundering. Key cases: Enron 2001, Bernie Madoff Ponzi scheme 2008 (largest $65B), Wells Fargo fake accounts 2016. Works with SEC, IRS-CI, and FinCEN. Post-2008 financial crisis focus increased on financial institution fraud.

National Security Letters (NSLs) are administrative subpoenas FBI issues for electronic communications transactional records, financial records, credit checks. No court approval needed. Includes gag order preventing recipient from disclosing. 2003-2006: FBI issued 192,000 NSLs. Inspector General found improper use. USA FREEDOM Act 2015 added some limits and reporting requirements.

FBI backdoor searches: querying NSA's Section 702 database for US person communications without warrant. 2021: 3.2M queries. FBI says these are for legitimate investigations. Privacy advocates say it is warrantless surveillance of Americans. Reforms limited some query types but 702 reauthorized 2024. Tension between collection authority and Fourth Amendment.

FBI overseen by DOJ Inspector General, Congress (HJC/SJC), Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board, FISC. Inspector General reports public and classified. Key IG findings: NSL misuse, FISA errors, Carter Page FISA flaws. FBI Director serves 10-year term to insulate from politics. Wray 2017-2025, Patel 2025-.

FBI investigated January 6 Capitol attack: largest investigation in FBI history. 1,400+ charged, 900+ sentenced. Cases ranged from trespassing to seditious conspiracy (Oath Keepers, Proud Boys leaders). Digital forensics: geolocation, social media, cell tower data identified suspects. FBI used face recognition despite policy concerns. Raised questions about domestic terrorism definition and First Amendment boundaries.

FBI seal: blue circle with gold border, scales of justice, shield, olive branch, 13 stars. Motto: Fidelity, Bravery, Integrity adopted 1935. Seal appears on credentials, buildings, official documents. Unauthorized use is federal crime. FBI flag flown at field offices. FBI has distinctive identity as both law enforcement and intelligence agency.
